title: Learned fetal MRI patterns associate with later motor development
summary: A fetal MRI study combined CNN-derived movement measures with learned brain coactivation patterns. It analyzed brain networks in 120 fetuses; CNN-based movement extraction succeeded in 98. One supplementary-motor/posterior coactivation pattern was associated with seven-month motor scores, while fetal movement itself was not significantly associated with postnatal motor outcomes. These observational relationships do not establish causal development or a validated individual prognostic test.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network; k-means coactivation clustering
organization: New York University; Wayne State University

source_review.scope: Primary relevant Methods/results/limitations, exact primary front identity and current primary PubMed notice metadata; version dates distinguished.

evidence.tested: CNN-derived head-motion measurements, k-means brain-state analysis and later Bayley motor-score associations.
evidence.unknown: Causal mechanisms, individual prognostic utility and independent replication remain unestablished; CNN failures reduced the movement sample.
evidence.ai_role: A CNN masks fetal brains for motion measurement, while k-means learns recurring low-motion fMRI coactivation states whose occurrence is related to development.
